questions.q: What is a routing address in Email-to-Case?
options: A Salesforce permission that controls who can view cases
The link between a real inbox your customers already use and a Salesforce-generated email services address
A validation rule that blocks spam from becoming cases
The folder where closed cases are archived
questions.explain: A routing address connects a real email address (like support@yourcompany.com) to the unique, generated address Salesforce actually receives mail at.

questions.q: After creating a routing address, what has to happen in your real email system for Email-to-Case to actually work?
options: Nothing — Salesforce reads the real inbox directly without any forwarding
The real address must be deleted
You must forward incoming mail from the real address to the generated *.case.salesforce.com address
Your email system needs a Salesforce-signed SSL certificate installed
questions.explain: Salesforce never reads your real mailbox directly — you configure your email system to forward messages to the generated email services address, which is what Salesforce actually receives.

questions.q: What does On-Demand Service let an org do that it couldn't do with just the legacy Email-to-Case Agent?
options: Receive inbound email directly without installing or maintaining any local, on-premise software
Create cases from phone calls instead of email
Skip creating a routing address entirely
Automatically close cases after 30 days
questions.explain: On-Demand Service is Salesforce's hosted delivery method — no local software required — which is why it's the standard choice for nearly every org today, versus the legacy on-premise Agent.

questions.q: In a case created by Email-to-Case, what does the inbound email's Subject line become?
options: The case Description
The Case Owner field
It's discarded and not stored anywhere
The Case Subject
questions.explain: The email's Subject line maps directly to the case's Subject field; the email body becomes the case Description.

questions.q: What does a Thread ID inserted in the email subject or body accomplish?
options: It encrypts the email for security
It matches a customer's reply back to the existing open case instead of creating a duplicate new one
It sets the case priority automatically
It assigns the case to a specific queue
questions.explain: The Thread ID is a token Salesforce inserts so that when a customer replies, Salesforce recognizes the reply belongs to an already-open case rather than spawning a new one.
